paragraphs: Katab rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hammitzvot tzarik haadam lizkor betok akilato churban habbayit kemo shekkatub bazzohar teruma, veyidag belibbo al zot shebbizman shebbet hammiqdash qayyam hayeta hashshekina meqabbelet shepa meulleh umeshubbach mimmah shehu achar churban, al ken yargil lomar leshem yichud qudesha berik hu ushekinetta veku' hareni zoker et yerushalayim asher chareba baaonotenu vahareni metzappeh lebinyanah sheyyibbaneh otah hqb"h bimhera beyamenu amen, vihi ratzon millepaneka Adonai elohenu velohe abotenu shettishkon betok yerushalayim irak kaasher dibbarta vekisse david abdeka mehera betokah takin ubeneh otah binyan olam bimhera beyamenu, veqayyam bah miqra shekkatub vaani ehyeh lah neum Adonai chomat esh sabib ulekabod ehyeh betokah: gam yizzaher lomar betok hasseuda pittum haqqetoret upereq ezehu meqoman, veaach"k yomar elohenu velohe abotenu melek rachaman rachem alenu tob umetib hiddaresh lanu veku' ad kebirkat Adonai eloheka asher natan lak aach"k yomar vetimlok atta Adonai elohenu mehera al kol maaseka behar tziyyon mishkan kebodeka ubirushalim ir qadasheka kakkatub bedibre qadasheka yimlok Adonai leolam elohayik tziyyon ledor vador halluyah, veqodem pittum haqqetoret upereq hannizkar yomar pesuqim ellu lehodot lehallel leshabbeach lepaer leromem lehadder ulenatztzeach al kol dibre david ben yishay abdeka meshichaka: baatzateka tancheni veachar kabod tiqqacheni: vehu rachum yekapper aon velo yashchit vehirba lehashib appo velo yair kol chamato: ashre haggeber asher teyasserennu yah umittorateka telammedennu: vaani bechasdeka batachti yagel libbi bishuateka ashira laAdonai ki gamal alay: sos asis baAdonai tagel napshi belohay ki hilbishani bigde yesha meil tzedaqa yeatani kechatan yekahen peer vekakkalla tadeh keleha: veyibtechu beka yodee shemeka ki lo azabta doresheka Adonai: simchu baAdonai vegilu tzaddiqim veharninu kol yishre leb: ner leragli debareka veor lintibati: odeka ki anitani vattehi li lishua: veaach"k yomar mizmor hayyom veaach"k hoshieni Adonai elohenu veku' ad veyimmale kebodo et kol haaretz amen veamen, veaach"k pittum haqqetoret veaach"k ezehu meqoman veaach"k en kelohenu veku':

clarification.explanation:
Our teacher the Ari z"l wrote (in Sha'ar HaMitzvot) that during his meal a person should remember the destruction of the Temple — as brought in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah) — and grieve in his heart that while the Temple stood, the Shechinah received a more lofty and superior flow of abundance than it does after the destruction. Therefore he should make a habit of saying 'for the sake of the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,' and after it: 'I hereby remember Jerusalem, which was destroyed because of our sins, and I hereby look forward to its rebuilding, may the Holy One, blessed be He, rebuild it speedily in our days, Amen,' along with the formula 'May it be Your will... that You dwell within Jerusalem Your city... and speedily establish within it the throne of David Your servant, and build it as an everlasting structure speedily in our days.'
He should also be careful to say during the meal 'Pittum HaKetoret' and the chapter 'Eizehu Mekoman'; and before them he should say the verses 'to give thanks, to praise, to glorify... concerning all the words of David son of Yishai, Your servant, Your anointed' (By Your counsel You guide me; And He, being merciful; Happy is the man; But I have trusted in Your kindness; I will greatly rejoice; And those who know Your name; Be glad in the Lord; Your word is a lamp; I will thank You), and after them the Psalm of the Day and 'Save us, Lord...'; and after 'Pittum HaKetoret' and 'Eizehu Mekoman' he should say 'Our God and God of our fathers, Merciful King... And You, Lord our God, shall speedily reign over all Your works, on Mount Zion the dwelling place of Your glory, and in Jerusalem Your holy city...' and 'Ein KeElokeinu.'
takeaways: During the meal, one should remember the destruction of the Temple and grieve over it — for the Shechinah then received a more lofty flow of abundance.
One should say 'Leshem Yichud,' the formula remembering Jerusalem, and the prayer for its rebuilding.
During the meal one should say Pittum HaKetoret and Eizehu Mekoman, along with the surrounding verses and prayers.

paragraphs: Tzarik lesheb bekabod al hashshulchan haddor bilbusho kemo sheyyosheb lipne gedolim, ubiprat beshaa shemmebarek birkat hammazon vekakkatub (shemot tv, b) zeh eli veanvehu vedareshu bazeh rashe tebot zeh hashshulchan asher lipne Adonai ukemo shekkatub bechesed lealpayim:

clarification.explanation: When a person sits down to eat at the table, he must sit with dignity and in proper, orderly attire, as though he were sitting before important and great people — especially at the time of Birkat HaMazon. The source for this is the verse 'Zeh Eli ve'anvehu' (This is my God and I will glorify Him), from which the Sages expounded, by way of an acronym: 'Zeh haShulchan asher lifnei Hashem' (This is the table that is before the Lord) — meaning that the table at which we eat is considered akin to an altar before the Lord, and therefore it should be treated with the respect due to it.
takeaways: One should sit at the table with dignity and in respectable attire, as if sitting before important people.
This should be observed especially at the time of Birkat HaMazon, since the table is considered like an altar before the Lord.

paragraphs: Minhag hachasidim qodem lekol seuda bime hachol yipneh techilla ubiprat im margish hitorerut begupo vedabar zeh hu tzorek gadol "p hassod, veyittol yadayv vibarek asher yatzar veaach"k yaamod veyitvaddeh beyom sheyyesh bo techinna, veyosheb bemaqom sherotzeh leekol veyishteh meat mayim pachot merebiit im taeb lammayim o yishteh meat shekar vikavven liptor mayim shebbetok hammazon, veaach"k yomar leshem yichud ubaqqashot sheamarnu leel veaach"k yittol yadayv kahalaka bishbil haakila, ubeyamim sheen bahem techinna sheen omerim vidduy yomru mizmor bebo elayv natan hannabi (tehillim n":b') viharher bitshuba belibbo vekol zeh yihyeh lo ezer vesiyyua el habberur sheoseh baakilato veayyen chesed laalapim siman qn"z ot t':

clarification.explanation: The custom of God-fearing people is that before every weekday meal, especially if they feel a bodily need, they should relieve themselves first — and this matter is very important according to the Kabbalah as well. Afterward he should wash his hands and recite the blessing 'Asher Yatzar,' and then, on days when confession (Vidui/Tachanun) is recited, he should stand and confess his sins. Before the meal itself he should sit in a fixed place, and drink a little water (less than a revi'it) if thirsty, or a little beer, with the intention of thereby exempting himself from the obligation to drink water during the meal. Afterward he should recite the formula of 'Leshem Yichud' and the petitions mentioned earlier, and only then wash his hands properly for the eating itself. On days when confession is not said, he should instead say Psalm 51 ('Beshevet Eilav Natan HaNavi' / 'When Nathan the Prophet came to him') and meditate in his heart on thoughts of repentance. All of this is meant to assist in the refinement of the holy sparks contained in the food, as is also mentioned in the book Chesed LaAlafim.
takeaways: It is good to relieve oneself before the meal, and to recite confession or at least Psalm 51 and meditate on repentance.
One should drink a little before eating to exempt the obligation of water, and recite the 'Leshem Yichud' formula before washing hands for the meal itself.

paragraphs: Asur litom ad sheyyitten maakol libhemto o chayya veop sheyyesh lo bebeto dimzonotehem alayv, diktib (debarim y, tv) "eseb besadeka libhemteka, veakalta vesabaetta". veraq bishtiyya haadam qodem labbehema diktib (bammidbar k, ch) "vehishqita et haeda veet beiram":

clarification.explanation: A person is forbidden to taste anything himself before he has given food to the animal, beast, or fowl in his possession for whose sustenance he is responsible — as it is said, 'grass in your field for your cattle, and you shall eat and be satisfied' (meaning: one gives to the animal first, and only afterward does the person himself eat). In contrast, regarding drinking the law is reversed — a person takes precedence over his animal in drinking, as it is said, 'and you shall give drink to the congregation and their livestock' (meaning: Moses gave drink first to the Children of Israel and only afterward to the animals).
takeaways: A person must feed the animals in his possession before he eats himself.
Regarding drinking, the order is reversed — a person may drink before he gives drink to his animals.

paragraphs: En mesichin bisuda shemma yaqdim qaneh leveshet, vedin zeh nizkar baggemara (taanit h:) venipsaq lahalaka bekol sipre harishonim za"l vegam beshulchan hattahor beli shum machaloqet, vekatab haggaon chida" bebirke yosep dela nimtza shum chakam vechasid shennizhar bedabar zeh, velaken dabar zeh belibbo keesh boeret leda mah zeh veal mah zeh venacha dato daat elyon betaam shekkekatab harab eliyya rabba za"l beshem happerisha debachalaqot yashit shebbizmannam hayu mesubbin baakilatam ushekicha hezzeqa, vehaiddana yattobe yatebinan kullam shavim veyamin usemol shaqolae ninehu, ukegon da lekka lemechash, vegabra rabba amar milleta demittabta data umistabbera kevateh ad kan debarayv, veayyen od lehaggaon hannizkar beshiyyure beraka mah shekkatab bedabar zeh yeuyyan sham, veek sheyyihyeh hinneh atta en lanu semek laabor al dibre chaza"l baddin hannizkar ki im raq lepi hattaam shel haggaon perisha za"l velaken belel pesach dekullanu mesubbin chayyabin min haddin lehizzaher bedabar zeh ukemo shekkatab harab za"l, vegam bishar yemot hashshana im yizdammen ezeh sibba leadam lihyot meseb al semolo veokel chayyab leqayyem dibre chaza"l hannizkarim shello yasicha:

clarification.explanation: One should not speak while there is food in the mouth during a meal, out of concern that the food might enter the windpipe (kaneh) instead of the esophagus (veshet) and cause choking — this law is already brought in the Gemara, tractate Ta'anit, and was ruled halachically by all the Rishonim and the Shulchan Aruch without any dissent. However, the Chida writes that in practice he found no sage or pious person who was actually careful in this matter, and this troubled him greatly until he found an explanation: in ancient times people ate while reclining on their side (leaning to the left, as was the custom of those reclining), and this position carried a greater risk of choking, so silence was required. But nowadays, when people sit upright and evenly, the danger is far smaller and there is no such concern. Nevertheless, despite this explanation, we have no authority to entirely nullify the words of our Sages, and therefore on the night of the Seder (when everyone reclines) one must be careful about this according to the original ruling, and likewise whenever anyone reclines on his left side for any reason, he must be careful not to speak during the meal.
takeaways: By strict law it is forbidden to speak while food is in the mouth, due to the danger of choking.
In practice one should be especially careful about this on the night of Pesach (when reclining) or whenever reclining on one's side.

paragraphs: Im betok seuddato rotzeh leekol perot velishtot yayin shetztzarik lebarek ak yadayv meluklakim battabshil, lo yebarek beyadayim mezohamot ella yittol yadayv o yeqannechem bemitpachat kede sheyyebarek al happerot o hayyayin binqiyyut ukemo shekkatab bechesed lealpayim: gam tzarik haadam lehizzaher bekamma hilkot derek eretz hashshayyakim lasseuda asher hizhiru otanu chaza"l bahem veellu hen, shenayim mamtinim zeh lazeh biqara, dehaynu keshehaechad mesalleq yadayv min haqqeara leezeh eseq az chabero mapsiq milleekol ad sheyyigmor isqo, abal im hem shelosha en hashshenayim poseqin bishbil haechad, vekol zeh ayri beshavim zeh im zeh abal im haechad meseb im abiv o im achiv haggadol o im mi sheggadol bechakema shechayyab bikbodo tzarik lehamtin lo, veen haggadol tzarik lehamtin laqqatan vekannizkar bechesed laalapim, mihu im yesh lipnehem tabshil veechad mehem silleq yado min haqqeara leezeh eseq sheim yamtin hashsheni yitqalqel hattabshil mechamat sheyyitqarer velo epshar leakelo, en tzarik lehamtin apillu qatan legadol:

clarification.explanation:
If in the middle of the meal one wishes to eat fruit or drink wine requiring a blessing, but his hands are soiled from the cooked food — he should not recite the blessing with dirty hands, but should wash his hands or wipe them with a cloth in order to recite the blessing in cleanliness (as written in Chesed LaAlafim).
One must also be careful about several laws of proper conduct (derech eretz) at the meal about which our Sages cautioned us: two people eating from one shared bowl wait for each other — when one removes his hand from the bowl for some matter, his companion stops eating until he finishes; but if there are three, the other two do not stop on account of the one. All this applies among equals; but if one is eating with his father, or his older brother, or someone greater than him in wisdom whose honor he is obligated to observe, he must wait for him, and the greater one need not wait for the lesser. Nevertheless, if the dish before them would spoil (cool down) and become inedible were the other to wait, there is no need to wait, even for a lesser person waiting for a greater one.
takeaways: Hands soiled from cooked food should be washed or wiped before reciting a blessing over fruit or wine.
Two people sharing a bowl wait for each other; three do not stop on account of one.
One waits for a father or someone greater in wisdom; but if the dish would spoil by waiting, there is no need to wait.

paragraphs: En mistakkelin bipne haokel velo bemah sheokel kede shello yitbayyesh, veim yesh lipne hamsubbin qeara achat melea sheokelim kullam mimmenna lo yitten acher mehamsubbin enayv bah libror mimmenna cheleq yapeh leatzmo ella yiqqach min habba beyado, vegam lo yoshit yado ella bemah shellepanayv, gam lo yiqqach beyado maneh gedola veyannicha lepanayv o yochazenna beyado veyokal mimmenna, veim okelim al yede kap lo yemalle hakkap al kol gedotayv veyannicha bepiv:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to stare at someone who is eating, nor even at what he is eating, so as not to cause him embarrassment. Likewise, when several people eat from one shared bowl, a person may not fix his eyes on the bowl in order to select for himself the finest piece, but must take whatever comes within his reach. He also may not reach his hand toward anything except what is directly in front of him in the bowl, and may not take a large piece and set it before himself or hold it in his hand and eat from it slowly. And one who eats with a spoon should not fill the spoon to its brim each time he puts it into his mouth.
takeaways: One must not stare at a person who is eating or at what he is eating, so as not to embarrass him.
When eating from a shared bowl, one should not select the best portion for himself, and should reach only for what is directly in front of him.

paragraphs: Yizzaher shello yetannep malbushayv baakelo, veim okel beyado lo yelaklek kol hayyadayim ella raq rashe etzbeotayv, vetob venaim shello yokal ella "y kap, velo yokal ella raq beyad achat velo bishte yadayim, velo yannicha legima gedola letok piv, ubeet shemmaknis hammaakol lepiv yizzaher shello yitlaklek sear zeqeno, veyizzaher lidchot sear sepamo lekan ulekan qodem ekilu kede shello yishtalshelu harbeh al sepatayv veyitlakkelu harbeh, ubekol debarim ellu yitnaheg apillu bebeto al shulchano vekol shekken keshehu okel im bene adam, vehammazmin orechim bebeto umebi lipnehem tabshil roteb veeno mebi lahem kappot leekol bahem hare zeh chote umezalzel bikbod haorechim:

clarification.explanation: One must be careful not to soil his garments while eating. Someone who eats with his hands should not soil his entire hand, only the tips of his fingers, and it is better and more pleasant to eat specifically with a spoon. One should eat with one hand only, not both hands together, and should not put too large a mouthful into his mouth at once. He must be careful not to soil his beard when bringing food into his mouth, and to push the hairs of his mustache aside before eating so that they do not become soiled with leftover food. These rules apply even when eating alone at home, and all the more so when eating in the company of others. And one who invites guests and serves them a dish with sauce without providing them spoons to eat with is considered a sinner and as demeaning the honor of his guests.
takeaways: One should be careful not to soil garments, hands, beard, or mustache while eating, and it is preferable to eat with a spoon.
A host must provide his guests with spoons when serving a dish with sauce, otherwise he demeans their honor.

paragraphs: Lo yemaher bilisato vaakilato ella yitnaheg leat leat, apillu im meseb im adam gargeran, veim habbasar qasheh lo yehe noshek beshinnayv umoshek beyadayv ella yesalleq yado mimmennu, velo yimtzotz etzbeotayv bepiv ben akila laakila, velo yireh chibba vechesheq al haakila, velo yemalle piv ella raq bikde sheyyukal ledabber besapa berura, velo yoshit yadayv liqara ad sheyyigmor libloa mah shebbepiv, veyapsiq meat ben leaseha achat leacheret, veim hamsubbin immo sillequ yedehem meoto maakol gam hu yesalleq yado "p sheadayin taeb leekol, delav orach ara leekol yechidi ben hamsubbin: velo yochaz yado perusa kabbetza veyokal, velo yishteh koso bebat achat beli shiyyur, ella yishteh keminhag hammedina, velo yishteh shette kosot zeh achar zeh velo yipshot yado biqara bipne mi sheggadol mimmennu apillu im yesh qeara bipne kol echad veechad, vekol haober al hilkot derek eretz hannizkarot leel vekayyotze bahem hare zeh reabtan gargeran missitra dehu deamar haliteni na (bereshit kh, l), vehinneh hu neechaz bassebak hassitra achara, veim hu baal tora veoseh ken hare zeh mechallel shem shamayim velaken ameru rabbotenu za"l (tanna debe eliyyahu rabba, ) derek eretz qadema lattora, vekaasher heeriku bazeh besipre hammusar vehayyira:

clarification.explanation: One should not hurry in chewing and eating, but should eat slowly, even when reclining with a gluttonous person. If the meat is too tough to bite, one should not bite it with the teeth and pull with the hands, but should withdraw his hand from it. He should not suck his fingers in his mouth between bites, and should not display excessive craving or fondness for the food. He should fill his mouth only to the extent that he can still speak clearly, and should not reach his hand into the bowl until he has finished chewing and swallowing what is already in his mouth, pausing briefly between one chew and the next. If the others reclining with him have stopped eating a certain food, he too must stop, even if still hungry, since it is not proper conduct to eat alone among those reclining together. He should not hold a whole slice the size of an egg and eat from it, nor drink an entire cup at once without pause, but according to the custom of the locality, nor drink two cups consecutively, nor reach his hand into the bowl in the presence of someone greater than himself, even if each has a separate bowl. Whoever transgresses these rules of proper conduct is considered a glutton and a gourmand, in the manner of Esau who said, 'Feed me now, I pray,' and he thereby becomes attached to the place of the Sitra Achra (the Other Side); and if he is a Torah scholar and behaves this way, it constitutes a desecration of the Divine Name. Therefore our Sages said that 'proper conduct precedes the Torah.'
takeaways: One should eat slowly and politely, without gluttony and without displaying craving for food.
These practices fall under the principle that 'proper conduct precedes the Torah' — neglecting them, especially for a Torah scholar, constitutes a desecration of the Divine Name.

paragraphs: Yitab libbo bisuddato im meat veim harbeh yokal pitto besimcha velo bekaas udeaga, veyizzaher leekol hattob vehammoil lo lirpua velo mah sheareb lo lepi shaa, veyishtaddel likbosh taavato baakila ushetiyya tamid, vekatebu chakme hammusar debehet hammaakol o hammashqeh lipne haadam vehu matoq lechikko vechabib alayv beyoter veyimshok yado mimmennu bishbil siggup lekapparat onot, hare zeh nechshab tiqqun gadol betiqqune hatteshuba veyesh bo toelet kemo hattaanit:

clarification.explanation: A person should eat his meal — whether little or much — with joy and not out of anger or worry. He should take care to eat what is good and beneficial for his health, not merely what is pleasant to the palate at that moment, and should always strive to conquer his desire for eating and drinking. The Sages of Mussar wrote that when a sweet and especially cherished food or drink is set before a person, and nevertheless he withdraws his hand from it for the sake of self-affliction and atonement for sins, this is considered a great achievement in the process of repentance, with a benefit comparable to that of fasting.
takeaways: One should eat with joy, not anger, and choose healthy foods rather than merely tasty ones.
Abstaining from a particularly beloved food for the sake of atonement is considered like a fast and a great achievement for the soul.

paragraphs: Lo yokal meummad velo yishteh meummad, laken apillu kos shel qiddush delel shabbat veyom tob shemmeqaddesh meummad, minhag rabbenu haari"y za"l achar birkat haqqadosh lesheb veyishteh hakkos, velo yashen samuk laakila, velo yaamod miyyad achar akila veyishheh keshiur beraka acharona shel otah akila, deim akal pat yashsheh bishibato shiur birkat hammazon, veim mezonot vekayyotze - shiur beraka meen shalosh:

clarification.explanation: One should not eat or drink while standing. Therefore even the cup of Kiddush on the night of Shabbat and Yom Tov, which is recited standing, the Ari z"l was accustomed, after the blessing of Kiddush, to sit and drink the cup while seated. One should not sleep close to eating, and should not get up immediately after eating, but should wait an amount of time equivalent to reciting the final blessing: if he ate bread, he should remain seated for the duration of Birkat HaMazon, and if he ate mezonot or the like, for the duration of the blessing me'ein shalosh.
takeaways: One should not eat or drink standing — even the cup of Kiddush should be drunk while seated.
After eating, one should remain seated at least until the time it takes to recite the final blessing.

paragraphs: Hanniknas lebet baal habbayit kol mah sheyyomar lo baal habbayit o gedol habbayit yaaseh, veyishheh meat keminhag hammedina, veen mesarebin laggadol, velo yomar hanniknas lebet chabero tenu li leekol ad sheyyomru hem, veraq bammayim yomar tenu li mayim lishtot:

clarification.explanation: One who enters the home of a host must do whatever the host or the head of the household tells him, and should wait a little according to the local custom before asking for anything. One does not refuse the greater person. A guest entering the home of his friend should not say on his own, 'Give me food to eat,' until they offer it to him; but regarding water, he is permitted to say, 'Give me water to drink.'
takeaways: A guest should wait to be offered food and not ask for it himself, though he may ask for water to drink.
One must obey the host or head of the household and not refuse him.

paragraphs: Lo yishshok perusa veyittenenna lipne chabero o letok haqqeara lepi sheen daat kol habberiyyot shava, velo yishteh mehakkos veyitten lachabero deshemma sheyyamut, ubetzavvaot rabbi eliezer haggadol mazhir shello lishtot mimmah sheshshiyyer chabero deshemma yesh lo choli veyitareb roq bepiv beoto shiyyur, umah shennohagim haolam litom bene habbayit mikkos shel haqqadosh shemmeqaddesh baal habbayit haynu mippene sheyyodeim shebbaal habbayit en bo choli sheyyazziq lahem, v"p sheameru behilkot derek eretz shello yishteh kos veyannichennu reqan al hashshulchan ella yochazennu beyado ad sheyyabo hashshemesh veyittenehu lo, mikkol maqom im minhag hammedina dela qapedi behaki gam hu lo yaqpid:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to bite off a piece and give it to one's companion, or return it to the shared bowl, since not everyone's sensibilities are the same (some might find it repulsive). It is also forbidden to drink from a cup and then give it to one's companion to drink from, out of concern that illness might be transmitted. And in the testament of Rabbi Eliezer HaGadol, a person is warned not to drink from what his companion has left over in his cup, lest the companion have an illness and his saliva has mingled with the leftover. As for the widespread custom of household members tasting from the host's Kiddush cup — this is because it is known to them that the host has no illness that could harm them. And likewise, although it was said in the laws of proper conduct not to leave an empty cup on the table but to hold it in one's hand until the attendant comes to take it, nevertheless if the local custom is not particular about this, one need not be particular either.
takeaways: One should not give another person a bitten piece to eat or the remains of a drunk cup, due to health concerns.
The custom of tasting from the host's Kiddush cup is a special and permitted exception, since it is known there is no risk of illness.

paragraphs: "p sheameru chakamim za"l leshayyer pea biqara min hattabshil, im kol zeh katab rabbenu za"l beshaar taame hammitzot deen din zeh noheg atta bazeh hazzeman ayyen sham, umikkol maqom lav orach ara leekol hammaakol kullo ad ba ad qitztzo, vekol shekken shello lihyot melachek pineke mishshum shurat derek eretz vekannizkar bechesed laalapim:

clarification.explanation: Although the Sages said to leave over a 'pe'ah' (a small portion of food) in the bowl and not finish it entirely, our teacher the Ari z"l wrote (in Sha'ar Ta'amei HaMitzvot) that this law does not apply nowadays. Nevertheless, it is not proper conduct to eat the food entirely to its very last bit, and certainly one should not be a 'plate-licker' — for the sake of proper conduct (as brought in Chesed LaAlafim).
takeaways: The law of leaving over a 'pe'ah' portion in the bowl — according to the Ari, does not apply in our time.
Nevertheless, proper conduct dictates not finishing the food entirely, and certainly not licking the plate.

paragraphs: Katab rabbenu mh"r chayyim veyittol za"l beshaar taame hammitzot haya noheg mori za"l peamim rabbot letzavvot libne beto sheyyabiu lepanayv isbe dedabra, sheen nizraim bide adam, o qotzim vedardarim shedderek bene adam leakelam vehaya okelam kede leqayyem beatzmo qillat adam harishon shennitqallel (bereshit g,ych) veqotz vedardar veku' veakalta veku' ayyen sham, upoh irenu y" epshar leqayyem debar zeh beisbe dedabra sheqqorin keeber (eseb bar qotzani) vehem domin leqotz vedardar vekobeshim otah bemayim umelach veneekalim, ak tzarik libdoq min hattolaim heteb heteb:

clarification.explanation: Rabbi Chaim Vital writes in the book Sha'ar Ta'amei HaMitzvot that the Ari z"l was often accustomed to instruct his household to bring him wild field herbs not sown by human hand, or thorns and thistles that people are accustomed to eat — and he would eat them in order to fulfill in himself the curse placed upon Adam HaRishon, 'thorn and thistle shall it bring forth for you... and you shall eat the herb of the field.' The Ben Ish Chai adds that in the city of Baghdad this custom can be fulfilled by means of a local thorny wild herb called 'ka'aber,' which resembles a thorn and thistle, and it is customarily pickled in water and salt and then eaten — though one must be careful to check it very thoroughly for worms.
takeaways: The Ari z"l would eat wild herbs and thorns in order to fulfill in himself the curse of Adam HaRishon, 'thorn and thistle shall it bring forth for you.'
In Baghdad this was fulfilled by means of a local wild herb ('ka'aber') pickled in water and salt, while taking great care to check it thoroughly for worms.

paragraphs: Im roeh okalim mushlakim baqqarqa asur lehannicham kak ella tzarik lahasiram mishsham, veken asur ligrom laokalim sheyyaasru bahanaa shello letzorek, vekol perot shennimasim "y zeriqa asur lezareqan apillu lipne chatan vekalla baabur simcha o simana taba, upoh irenu osin lipamim belel hammila shulchan munnach alayv anapim uperachim murkabim zeh al gab zeh lenoy, vegobelin issa shel qemach kede litchob betokah haanapim, vegam mebiim peri sheqqorin nome (limonit metuqa) shehu matoq o rimmon vekayyotze kede litchob bahem haanapim leherkebam zeh al gab zeh, uperot ellu vadday hem nimasim umitqalqelim bekak, vetzarik limchot bahem shello yaasu kazot beshum maakol uperot im yihyu mitqalqelim venimasim:

clarification.explanation: One who sees food thrown on the ground is forbidden to leave it that way, but must remove it, out of respect for the food. Likewise it is forbidden to cause food to become forbidden in benefit without need. Any fruit that becomes spoiled and repulsive through being thrown — it is forbidden to throw it, even before a bride and groom for the sake of rejoicing or as a good omen. The Ben Ish Chai mentions that in their city (Baghdad) it was sometimes the custom on the night of a circumcision to decorate a table with branches and flowers, and for this purpose they would knead a dough of flour in which to stick the branches, and they also used sweet fruits (such as a sweet citrus or pomegranate) to stick the branches into for decoration — but these fruits certainly become spoiled and ruined by this, and therefore one must protest against those who follow this practice, that they should not do so with any food or fruit if it will cause it to be spoiled.
takeaways: It is forbidden to leave discarded food on the ground — it should be picked up and not treated with disrespect.
It is forbidden to use fruit for decorative purposes (such as at a circumcision) if doing so causes it to spoil and become ruined.

paragraphs: En someke qeara melea bappat shemma yishshapek mimmenna al happat veyimmaes, veen lizroq pat meechad leechad "p sheeno nimas bizriqa, gam yesh bene adam kesheyyaasu perot kebushim beme umelach yannichu betokam chatikat pat kede sheyyihyeh lakkebushin taam yapeh vachatikat pat zo nimeset umitqalqelet vetzarik limchot beyadam bedabar zeh, vekol adam tzarik lekabbed et hallechem vealayv tabo birkat tob:

clarification.explanation: One should not rest a full bowl upon bread, out of concern that liquid might spill from it onto the bread and render it repulsive. One should not toss bread from hand to hand between people, even though it does not actually become repulsive from the tossing. Likewise, some people, when making pickled fruits (in salt water), place a piece of bread inside to give the pickles a better flavor — but that piece of bread becomes repulsive and spoiled, and one must protest against those who do this. And as a general rule, every person must treat bread with honor, for it is said that guarding the honor of bread brings a blessing.
takeaways: One should not toss bread or cause it to become soiled and repulsive, such as by resting a bowl on it or using it to pickle fruit.
One must treat bread with special honor — guarding its honor brings blessing.
